newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soy exports, China buying seen hot through fall.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soy exports, China buying seen hot through fall.

text.p: U.S. soybean exports, which have been posting new weekly records, will stay brisk through the fall and into next year until the South American bean crop enters the world markets, government analysts said Thursday.
Hot demand from China -- which has sparked huge export sales of U.S. soybeans and soybean meal -- is not expected to cool down for several weeks, the analysts said.

"We're the only soybean source in town at the moment," said Jim Matthews, head of the Agriculture Department's soybean estimates panel. "We expect our soybean exports to look good over the fall months, especially with China buying early on."
U.S. soybean and soybean meal export sales are running well ahead of last year's pace.

As of Oct. 17, U.S. soybean sales this marketing year totalled 7.502 million metric tons vs. 5.606 million last year at this time. Soybean meal sales totalled 1.588 million tons, twice last year's pace of 736,000 tons.
Soybean and soybean meal sales to China have soared in the past few weeks.

According to government figures, China has already bought 442,800 tons of U.S. soybeans, compared with only 50,000 tons at this time last year, and had booked 426,000 tons of U.S. bean meal vs. nothing at this point in 1995.
"China is the predominate business for U.S. soybeans right now. It is far and away the growth market," said Mark Ash with the Agriculture Department's Economic Research Service.

Matthews and Ash said due to a lower soybean crop in China, increased protein demand from China's livestock industry, lower U.S. prices, and currently tight South American supplies, China will likely continue to be a strong force in the U.S. market for the next several weeks.
The Agriculture Department is estimating Chinese soybean and soybean meal imports this marketing year at record levels.
Chinese soybean purchases in 1996/97 are currently pegged at 900,000 tons, up from 700,000 last year and compared to only 150,000 as recently as 1994/95.

Most of those soybeans will come from the United States. Last year China bought 423,000 tons of U.S. soybeans. This year analysts said it could buy up to 700,000 tons and maybe more from the United STates.

Chinese soybean meal imports are projected at 1.4 million tons, up from 1.1 million tons last year, and almost nothing before that. Although China buys most of its meal from South America, it will take a much bigger share from the United States this year, analysts said.
China is not the only bright spot in U.S. soybean exports, analysts said.

Taiwan has been an active buyer of U.S. soybeans this fall, already buying 907,000 tons compared to 497,000 tons last year at this time. Mexico has bought 586,000 tons of U.S. beans this year vs. last year's pace of 256,000.
Brazil, the top soybean competitor to the United States, could be in the market this fall for up to 500,000 tons of U.S. beans this fall, said the Agricultural Department's Matthew.
